title: Hanging backend: timeouts instead of errors
question: Why does a backend that hangs hurt more than one that refuses connections?
description: Server B stops answering instead of crashing cleanly. Requests sent to it wait for the full client timeout, and health probes wait for their own timeout too, so detection is slower.
assumptions: Abstract request-level model: no TCP, TLS, packets or real HTTP proxy semantics.
Each server has fixed concurrency slots and a FIFO queue; there is no CPU, memory or GC model.
Health probes bypass the request queue and answer instantly when the server is up.
Servers do not know when a client gave up; they finish the work and the late response is discarded.
No retries: every failed request is final.
Numbers are scenario inputs, not measured performance of any product.
expectedObservations: Requests sent to the hanging server fail only after the full 1000 ms client timeout instead of failing at once.
Latency of successful requests stays at the service time; the cost shows up in the p95 of all ended requests, which jumps to the timeout.
Detection takes longer than in the refuse case because each probe waits for its own timeout.
